1.

This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioners mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (North-West) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, intended to acquire about 2480 Bigha 01 Biswas of land with its specification Hem Chander (1605-06) vs Union Of India (Mubarakpur Dabas) on 11 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69176738/

The Government vide consequent Declaration/notification No. F.11(20)/2004/L&B/LA/28176 dated 19.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 2480 Bigha 01 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Mubarakpur Dabas, Delhi.

The LAC (N/W) after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no. 16 of 2005-06 dated 14.09.2005 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 2480 bighas 01 biswas out of the aforesaid said land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/- per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/- per bigha) for the entire said land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests.

4. It is stated that the petitioner is the recorded owner/bhumidhar in possession of having full share in the land bearing Khasra no.2/23(3-09), 4/3/1(4-02) situated in the revenue estate of Village Rani Khera, Delhi (in short, the said land).
5.
It is stated that the petitioners are entitled to receive the compensation amount of the actual prevailing market value of the said land.

The actual physical possession of the said land is with the petitioner as the physical possession of the land has not been taken and the respondents shall take possession thereof from the petitioners.

The ld. LAC passed the award in a mechanical way without applying the mind and without going through the claim filed by the petitioners, as such the award is not acceptable to the petitioner, and they has received the awarded amount under protest and without prejudice to their rights.

The LAC failed to take note of the actual and LAC no. 107 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Hem Chander. v. Union of India Page no. 3 of 11 practical market value of the said land and had adopted a narrow approach while observing that no proof of claim market value is attached.

sentences.text: The LAC has not assessed the actual market value of the said land in spite having knowledge of the fair market value adjudicated by the courts.
The LAC has failed to properly appreciate the quality, status, potentiality and development of the said land and its surroundings.

6. It is stated that the said land is well connected with the transport, telecommunication, roads and have all the basic amenities in and around the surrounding areas i.e. Mundka railway station is 11/2 kms away from the said land, Mundka Udyog Vihar Extension is located at a distance of about 2.5 kms away from the said land, where commercial activities are carried out and reputed clubs and party lawns are located within a radius of 2-4 kms away from the said land; godown of Food Corporation of India is at a distance of 3.5 kms away from the said land, District Sports School and the bottling plant of Indian Oil Corporation and Fortunes World's biggest 500 companies are at a distance of 3.5 kms away from the said land, NH-10 is at a distance of 2 kms away from the said land and Azad Hind Gram is at a distance of 4 - 5 kms away from the said land.

Co- LAC no. 107 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Hem Chander. v. Union of India Page no. 4 of 11 operative bank at Ghewra are located at a distance of 3 to 5 km from the said land.

sentences.text: 8. It is stated that the situation of the above stated areas shows the great importance in assessing the market value of the said land, and the similarly situated land was sold @ Rs. 2000/- per square yards by the vendors, therefore, the said land, which could easily fetch the same rate and the said land cannot be granted the market value less than Rs. 2000/- per sq. yards.
As such the ld. LAC has failed to take note of the judicial pronouncements and the government policy of 10% yearly escalation in the market value of the said land.

9. It is stated that the respondent no.2 has allotted the adjoining Rohini residential land to persons for residential as well as commercial purposes for more than Rs. 6000/- per square yards and that too, only to those who has applied for the plots/flats and shops well in advance, which fact shows that that the land for residential and commercial purposes was not easily available at the rate of Rs.
6000/- per square yards.

The respondent no.2 has been allotting the plots at the remotest and undeveloped the land, therefore, it is clear that the respondent no.2 cannot gain/earn profit at the cost of causing loss to the petitioner.
10. The ld. LAC, while passing the award has erred in not taking into account the devaluation of the money.
The ld. LAC should have taken note of the loss and injury suffered by the petitioner.

The ld.
LAC has grossly erred in LAC no. 107 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Hem Chander. v.
Union of India Page no. 5 of 11 directing the deduction of tax, from the amount of compensation of the said land as no tax from the amount of compensation and interest thereupon could be deducted.
It is stated that the petitioner has claimed the compensation for the acquire land @ Rs.2000/- per square yards in addition to Rs. 25,000/- per bigha, solatium amount along with interest.

24. The petitioners have not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioners.

25. Vide order dated 28.08.2023, the application under Order XXII Rule 3 CPC and u/s 5 of the Limitation Act was allowed subject to the condition that LRs of Late Sh. Hem Chander shall not be entitled to interest for the period from 31.05.2022 to 05.07.2023.

Thus, in view of this, the interest amount for the period w.e.f 31.05.2022 to 05.07.2023 shall not be entitled to LRs of deceased Hem Hem Chander (1605-06) vs Union Of India (Mubarakpur Dabas) on 11 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69176738/
5 Chander.
ISSUE NO. 2/ RELIEF 26.

In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioners are granted the following reliefs:-
LAC no. 107 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Hem Chander. v. Union of India Page no. 10 of 11 (1)
Fair Market value of land of petitioners as mentioned in the revised statement u/s 19 of the Act @ Rs.19,45,800/- per acre.
An enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/- per acre is accordingly accorded.
(2) Additional amount @ 12% ( in terms of Section 23 (1A) of the Act).
(3) Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation (in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).

(4) Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
27.
Reference petition is accordingly, answered with parties to bear their own respective costs.
